A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central theorems, experiments, and appendices A–J. The text, equations, figures, and table support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLP and Pythia experiments in Section 6, with additional empirical results in Appendices H and I.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including alignment accuracies, representation-distance measurements, and generalisation analyses.

M1.justification: The greedy identity alignment, orthogonal linear alignment, RevNet alignment, and DAS training objective remain unchanged. The revised abstraction definitions concern the formal framework rather than a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate hierarchical equality, indirect object identification, and the appendix distributive-law task. The IOI scenario using disjoint training and evaluation names already appears in v1.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same identity, linear, and nonlinear alignment comparisons and unmodified-DNN accuracy references. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix I retain the same model configurations, checkpoints, data splits, sample counts, intervention procedures, training budgets, and IIA evaluation metric. Relocated experimental descriptions do not introduce new protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the alignment-capacity and intervention-size sweeps, training-progression analyses, MLP injectivity investigation, IOI robustness and name-generalisation tests, and controls using DNNs trained to follow particular algorithms.

E5.justification: The reporting practices are retained: ten-run maxima and means with 95% confidence intervals in the relevant bar plots, five-seed analyses, and ten-seed means and standard deviations in Table 1.

E6.justification: The empirical plots in Figures 2–4 and 8–17 and the values in Table 1 are unchanged. Both versions report high alignment on randomly initialised models and failure of IOI alignment to generalise to unseen names for the randomly initialised model.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the foundational Definition 1 by adding a surjective input map and requiring corresponding model and algorithm computations to agree under every allowed intervention, through new Equation 6. v2 also explicitly excludes inputs from the internal state spaces and propagates this distinction through the definitions and Appendix F. This substantively strengthens the formal criterion, although the theorem statements and most proof reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claim that unrestricted alignment makes causal abstraction uninformative under the stated assumptions. The nonlinear representation dilemma and the empirical claims about alignment without task competence remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds explicit caveats about neural collapse and finite precision, softens the practical output-surjectivity statement, and explains why task correctness is necessary for perfect IIA when non-intervened inputs are included. Section 7 adds a distinction between supervised and unsupervised probing’s complexity trade-off.

D1.justification: Appendices A, I, and J retain the same code-access instructions, hyperparameters, precision adjustments, data-generation details, and CPU/A100 resource reporting. Their relocation adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Nikolaou et al. (2025) on transformer injectivity, including after training, and Papyan et al. (2020) on neural collapse. These locally extend the discussion of assumptions; the broader positioning and Appendix C remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a self-contained restatement of Definition 7 in Appendix F.2, shifting the existing lemmas to F.3. It also makes limited introduction, limitations, contribution, and acknowledgment edits and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information.

P2.justification: Figure 6 revises intervention arrows and neuron labels. Several existing appendix figures are repositioned, including Figures 10, 12, and 14–16, with accompanying page reflow. No empirical figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs Definition 1’s missing intervention-consistency requirement and clarifies inputs versus internal states. The largely retained Appendix F proof already targeted that consistency in v1, so the gain chiefly concerns formal specification and clarity. More careful assumption caveats and the self-contained definition further improve readability, while the empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
